GAMEPLAY.kind: fetched IGN/PortForward guides and inspected stills
GAMEPLAY.scope: Rope, water, gravity, pressure-door jamming and oscillatory platforms

contracts.behavior: A character can climb a hanging rope, swing using directional input, and jump off. A weighted sinking rope can operate a gate.
contracts.implemented: Constraint-based climbing/swing/release to an elevated ledge; the separate rope-operated gate puzzle is not implemented.

contracts.behavior: Position a floating object, expose the covered opening, operate a water mechanism, then board/use it as the changing water level raises it toward an exit.
contracts.implemented: Sliding cover and one valve-controlled rising basin; bounded water-area transfer, buoyancy, player load and drowning. No automatic rowing.

contracts.behavior: A timed switch activates an inverted field which deactivates without a second switch. Player and boxes change acceleration; mid-air timing matters.
contracts.implemented: Five-second temporary inversion, airborne reactivation, acceleration reversal without velocity reset; duration and units chosen for ECHO.

contracts.behavior: Increasingly rapid beeps warn of a timed gravity change.
contracts.implemented: Original synthesized cue with decreasing intervals before expiry; not the original beep count, waveform or automatic alternating final sequence.

contracts.behavior: Move boxes to trigger mechanisms and jam closing doors; alternate between platform edges to build oscillation and depart at a useful phase.
contracts.implemented: Surface-contact pressure gate with physical box jamming, and passive restoring seesaw driven by alternating player runs/jumps. Geometry, joint model and thresholds remain ECHO choices.

contracts.behavior: Independent magnet and gravity controls hold the first contacted block high while returning the second low. A separately documented field variant affects boxes without affecting the player.
contracts.implemented: Sixth room combines those reported ideas: manually reversed box-only force, solid ceiling contact capture with removable finite-force constraints, and a returned block used as a physical step. Guided blocks, heights and timing are ECHO choices. Upward momentum can outlast a field reversal.

limitations: Guides report gameplay on 2010 releases; the supplied Windows build was not executed or instrumented.
GameSpy groups the game into 24 chapters, unlike the package's chapter map; numbers are source-local labels, not proven one-to-one mappings.
Compiled declarations are not execution bodies, and annotations are not proven level-instance values.
No exact geometry, coefficients, original timestep, solver, periodic gravity phase, destructible box, ball-assisted buoyancy, magnetic force law or gun behavior is claimed.
No art/audio from the reference or walkthrough screenshots is included in playable assets.
